Lessons.Title: Multi-step Measurement Problems with Fractions
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will solve multi-step measurement problems involving whole numbers, fractions, and multiplicative comparisons.

Measurement problems can combine unit relationships, elapsed time, fractional quantities, and comparisons such as “times as much.” Solve one relationship at a time, keep units attached to quantities, and use intermediate results in the next step.
Core relationship: Fractional measurement and time durations. Split one hour into equal minute parts, then solve a multi-step total.

Local publisher 2021 source lesson activities: Warm-up:  True or False: Some Number Times a Fraction	 (10 minutes); Activity 1:  Info Gap: Noah’s School Day (Part 1)	 (15 minutes); Activity 2:  Info Gap: Noah’s School Day (Part 2)	 (20 minutes); Activity 3:  Shopping List	 [OPTIONAL] (20 minutes); Cool-down:  Oatmeal Raisin Cookies	 (5 minutes)
Source-aligned Edulytics model: How many minutes are in one quarter of an hour?
First-party Cool-down (not gated original): How many minutes are in three quarters of an hour?
Original visual/physical and peer-explanation activities still require teacher review.

KeyConcepts.Title: Fractional measurement and time durations
KeyConcepts.Rule: Split one hour into equal minute parts, then solve a multi-step total.
KeyConcepts.Example: How many minutes are in one quarter of an hour?

KeyConcepts.Title: Mathematical relationship
KeyConcepts.Definition: Fractional measurement conversions preserve a consistent whole unit.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Fractional measurement conversions preserve a consistent whole unit.
KeyConcepts.Example: A strip is 1/2 m and another 75 cm. Total length in cm?

KeyConcepts.Title: Exact inverse and unit check
KeyConcepts.Definition: Express fractions of metres as centimetres when applying a whole-number scale.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Express fractions of metres as centimetres when applying a whole-number scale.
KeyConcepts.Example: Three equal ropes measure 1/4 m each. What is their total in cm?

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Confusing one fourth of an hour with 25 minutes.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: It changes the unit, place value, or operation.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Split one hour into equal minute parts, then solve a multi-step total.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Adding metres and centimetres without conversion.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The comparison ratio or measurement units do not match the task.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Convert fractional metres and centimetres to a common unit.
